title: Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: We hereby certify that both the statement and the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis are correct.
quotes.for: The communities certify both the theorem statement and its proof.
Publication date of the Lean and Mathlib joint certification statement.

quotes.text: Joint statement by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative.
quotes.for: Endorsement of the joint verification statement by the Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative.

quotes.text: On November 20, 2026, Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as a Lean library comprising 17 million lines of code.
quotes.for: Release date of November 20, 2026 and size of 17 million lines of code.

quotes.text: The codebase depends directly only on Mathlib. Over the past day, the Lean and Mathlib communities have rallied to verify the proof's correctness.
quotes.for: Direct dependency only on Mathlib and community verification effort.

quotes.text: Crucially, the community has added a file that isolates the statement of the Riemann Hypothesis and imports only Mathlib.
quotes.for: Isolation of Mathlib's Riemann Hypothesis statement in a separate challenge file.

quotes.text: That statement was compared against the theorem proved by Alpöge using two independent tools (comparator and con-leche –compare), both confirming that the theorem proved in Alpöge’s library is exactly Mathlib’s statement of the Riemann Hypothesis.
quotes.for: Independent comparison tools comparator and con-leche --compare matching Alpöge's theorem to Mathlib's statement.

quotes.text: The checkers con-leche and con-ron come with a formal proof, relative to set theory, that they cannot accept a false proof, thus addressing concerns that Lean’s logic itself might have flaws that the proof could exploit.
quotes.for: Formal soundness proofs relative to set theory for con-leche and con-ron.

quotes.text: These checks ran on an inert export of the proof, out of reach of hypothetical malicious code in the Lean proof sources.
quotes.for: Verification performed on an inert proof export insulated from source code execution.

title: A remark on the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions.
quotes.for: Alpöge attributes the formalized argument to his collaboration with Claude.

quotes.text: This argument is a descendant of Stepanov’s, but multiplicity is hard to find over the integers, corresponding to something like differentiating whole numbers.
quotes.for: The proof's mathematical lineage as a descendant of Stepanov's function-field argument.

quotes.text: The simple, new, Fourier-analytic ideas in the toy setting led us to examine chaining theta lifts if we were to have the same tricks recur but work in a natively automorphic manner.
quotes.for: Fourier-analytic ideas and chaining theta lifts in a natively automorphic manner.

quotes.text: The argument is incredibly long at the moment, and while its formalization is finished and it is routine to produce a huge, unreadable document containing sufficient detail, in my view of my path I have just taken a step.
quotes.for: Why Alpöge did not release a machine-generated prose document alongside the finished formalization.

quotes.text: I intend to do my best to understand and impart understanding of this argument and its certain simplifications, to speak about it, to write it properly.
quotes.for: Alpöge's commitment to understand, simplify, and write a proper mathematical exposition.

quotes.text: This puts us in the rather extraordinary situation this age has made possible, in which I am presenting the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighbourhood around its mathematics.
quotes.for: Releasing a complete formal argument before mastering the surrounding mathematical neighborhood.

quotes.text: The precise timing is horrible. If I could have, I’d have finished this all much earlier.
quotes.for: Alpöge's remark on the timing of the discovery.

title: Verification files for the Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: The published Lean source compiles without errors, the five headline theorems depend only on the three standard axioms
quotes.for: Sutherland reports successful compilation and itemizes verification results.

quotes.text: Andrew Sutherland (MIT), checks run with Claude Code. Page last updated 2026-11-23 14:35 UTC. Results below are as of that time and this page will be updated as the remaining checks finish.
quotes.for: Update date of Sutherland's verification page and ongoing status of remaining checks.

quotes.for: Total module count of 175,187 compiled modules.

quotes.for: Verification runtime and thread count for the independent Rust kernel nanoda.

quotes.for: Declaration count, verification runtime, and thread count for con-leche.

quotes.text: "GRH" here means Dirichlet L-functions: all moduli and all characters. Dedekind zeta functions, Hecke L-functions and automorphic L-functions in general are not among the statements that were checked.
quotes.for: Scope of the verified Generalized Riemann Hypothesis statements and excluded L-function families.

quotes.text: As a check that does not depend on Mathlib's definition of the zeta function, the proof was combined with kimihiro64/Robin1984 (commit acab1a3), an independent formalization of Robin's and Lagarias's criteria on the same Lean and Mathlib versions.
quotes.for: Verification of Robin's and Lagarias's elementary divisor-sum criteria independent of Mathlib's zeta definition.

quotes.text: Importing both gives two theorems about the divisor sum, with no hypotheses and no mention of zeta
quotes.for: Unconditional divisor-sum inequalities derived with no mention of the zeta function.

quotes.text: The exported proof: output of lean4export on module Main. Unpacks to 61,570,595,788 bytes.
quotes.for: Unpacked byte size of the exported proof.

quotes.text: lean.tar.gz, the 14 parts from alpo.ge joined; 239,275,554 bytes
quotes.for: The 14-part source archive released on Alpöge's site.

quotes.text: We then repeated the build on a separate machine with lake build Main inside a bubblewrap sandbox: no network, the source tree read-only, only .lake writable, the archive downloaded afresh from the author's site, and Mathlib's files checked against the official cache first.
quotes.for: Independent offline rebuild inside a bubblewrap sandbox.

quotes.text: The export made inside that sandbox is byte-identical to the published one, so every check on the published export applies to it.
quotes.for: Sandboxed rebuild reproducing the published proof export byte for byte.

quotes.text: The Riemann hypothesis tells us about the deviation from the average.
quotes.for: The significance of the hypothesis for the distribution of primes.

quotes.text: Formulated in Riemann’s 1859 paper, it asserts that all the ‘non-obvious’ zeros of the zeta function are complex numbers with real part 1/2.
quotes.for: Riemann's 1859 formulation and the real part 1/2 condition for non-obvious zeros.

quotes.text: The Riemann hypothesis asserts that all interesting solutions of the equation ζ(s) = 0 lie on a certain vertical straight line. This has been checked for the first 10,000,000,000,000 solutions.
quotes.for: Computational verification for the first 10,000,000,000,000 solutions.

quotes.text: A proof that it is true for every interesting solution would shed light on many of the mysteries surrounding the distribution of prime numbers.
quotes.for: Clay Mathematics Institute's conditional phrasing on its active problem page.

title: Likely solution to Riemann hypothesis by AI marks turning point for mathematics

quotes.text: It wouldn't have any practical implications (at least not immediately)
quotes.for: Thomas Bloom cautions against expecting immediate practical applications.

title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem

quotes.text: First published on Sat 21 Nov 2026 16.39 GMT
quotes.for: Publication date of The Guardian report.

quotes.text: Levent Alpöge, a Turkish American mathematician, on Friday posted a note on his personal website saying that Claude, the AI software, had helped prove the Riemann hypothesis. He says that Claude helped develop a solution to the problem during the course of about six weeks.
quotes.for: Alpöge developing the proof with Claude over roughly six weeks.

quotes.text: Alpöge’s note was published just one day after Anthropic went public on the Nasdaq stock market index. He acknowledged that, writing: “The precise timing is horrible. If I could have, I’d have finished this all much earlier.”
quotes.for: Release timing one day after Anthropic's Nasdaq stock market debut.

quotes.text: The Riemann hypothesis is one of the seven Millennium prize math problems selected in 2000 by the Clay Mathematics Institute. The institute has offered $1m for each problem solved.
quotes.for: Selection among the seven Millennium Prize Problems in 2000 and the $1m prize.
